Thanks Irene — happy to set this up. Two options for the candidate environment:

1) CoderPad (preferred): quick to spin up, supports PyTorch snippets, no env install for candidate, easy recording of console output. We use a short starter repo + hidden unit tests.
2) Gitpod / ephemeral devbox: more realistic but riskier for timeboxed interviews due to dependencies.

I recommend CoderPad for a 75-minute hybrid session. If everyone agrees, I'll:
- create a CoderPad session (no sign-in required for candidate)
- attach the proctoring checklist to the invite
- include a short troubleshooting note (browser/disable extensions)

Proctoring checklist attached: proctoring-checklist.pdf
CoderPad: https://coderpad.io/session/ABCD-1234
Playbook: https://notion.redwood.ai/ops/proctor-playbook

Ben — any special test cases or starter code you prefer? Also, can you confirm if you'd like screen share for the debrief or just audio?

Debrief rubric (short):
- Correctness (0–4): passes unit tests / edge cases
- Modeling intuition (0–4): loss/regularization choices, overfitting discussion
- Systems thinking (0–3): inference latency/serving constraints, batching, KV cache ideas
- Communication (0–3): clarity, trade-offs, next steps

I'll attach the rubric doc: ml-debrief-rubric.md and create the calendar invite once Ivy confirms the exact time. I prefer screen share for the 25m debrief so we can sketch quick diagrams.
